label: proof; unreviewed
statement: Let R be a four-dimensional Bessel process started at r>0. For every S>0, E[R_S^(-2)]=(1-exp(-r^2/(2S)))/r^2, while E[sup_{0<=s<=S} R_s^(-2)]=infinity. More precisely, if tau_b is the first hitting time of b in (0,r), then lim_{b down to 0} P(tau_b<=S)/b^2=exp(-r^2/(2S))/r^2.
source_quote: Under Theorem6.4, does L2 convergence of initial conditions imply L2(Omega;L2(0,T;V) intersect C([0,T];H)) convergence of solutions?

label: proof; unreviewed
statement: For the Ito SDE dU=(U-U^3)dt+sqrt(2)U^2 dW with U_0=a>0, its global strong solution has E U_t^2=e^(2t) a^2 [1-exp(-1/(4 a^2 s(t)))], where s(t)=(e^(2t)-1)/2, for t>0. For every T>0, E sup_{t<=T} U_t^2=infinity. Thus solutions with deterministic initial values a_n=1/n cannot converge to the zero solution in L^2(Omega;C([0,T];R)), despite a_n tending to zero in L^2. This is an unreviewed candidate application to the general numbered Agresti-Veraar Problem 5; it makes no claim about extra hypotheses in the surrounding prose or present openness.
source_quote: Under Theorem6.4, does L2 convergence of initial conditions imply L2(Omega;L2(0,T;V) intersect C([0,T];H)) convergence of solutions?

label: proof; unreviewed
statement: For n>=3 let m_n=floor(n/log n), and let D_n be diagonal with m_n diagonal entries 1/n and n-m_n entries 1. Its empirical singular-value measure converges weakly to delta_1 and its smallest singular value is exactly 1/n, but for every fixed epsilon in (0,1), lim_n (1/n) sum_{s_i(D_n)<epsilon} |log s_i(D_n)|=1. Therefore a polynomial lower bound on the minimum, even if deterministic, does not alone establish the logarithmic uniform integrability used in Hermitization.
source_quote: Upgrade the convergence in probability of the empirical spectral distribution of n^{-1/alpha} X (i.i.d. entries in the domain of attraction of an alpha-stable law, alpha in (0,2)) to almost-sure weak convergence to mu_alpha.

label: proof; unreviewed
statement: If random variables Z_n valued in a metric space satisfy d(Z_n,z) tending to zero in probability for a deterministic z, then some deterministic increasing subsequence n_k satisfies Z_{n_k} tending to z almost surely. This does not upgrade the full sequence: independent Bernoulli variables with P(Z_n=1)=1/n converge to zero in probability but equal one infinitely often almost surely.
source_quote: Upgrade the convergence in probability of the empirical spectral distribution of n^{-1/alpha} X (i.i.d. entries in the domain of attraction of an alpha-stable law, alpha in (0,2)) to almost-sure weak convergence to mu_alpha.

statement: Let X be an iid complex-entry matrix array. Assume 0<alpha<2, lim_{t to infinity} t^alpha P(|X_11|>=t)=1, and that the conditional law of X_11/|X_11| given |X_11|>=t converges to a probability measure on the unit circle. If the entry law has a bounded density on C, Bordenave and Chafai, Around the circular law, arXiv:1109.3343, Theorem 6.2, printed page 39, already gives almost-sure weak convergence of the empirical eigenvalue measure of n^(-1/alpha) X to mu_alpha. The unrestricted upgrade is the subsequent remark; the bounded-density special case is not open in this cached source. The stated tail normalization is part of the source model, and present openness without the density assumption is unverified.
source_quote: Upgrade the convergence in probability of the empirical spectral distribution of n^{-1/alpha} X (i.i.d. entries in the domain of attraction of an alpha-stable law, alpha in (0,2)) to almost-sure weak convergence to mu_alpha.

label: proof; unreviewed
statement: Let X be a nearest-neighbor walk on Z whose conditional probability of stepping right at every time is at least p_*>1/2 almost surely. Then liminf_n X_n/n >= 2p_*-1 almost surely (for any fixed finite X_0). This applies to cookie environments with every site and every cookie at least p_*, including infinite stacks. It is a special case with infinite total cookie drift, and does not establish the finite-delta threshold in Kosygina-Zerner Problem 5.3.
source_quote: Can the assumption (BD) (bounded cookie stacks) in the one-dimensional ballisticity criterion of Theorem 5.2 (positive speed iff delta > 2) be replaced by (POS1) (all cookies push to the right) with unbounded stacks?

label: proof; unreviewed
statement: On the deterministic rooted b-ary tree, b>=2, let iid vertex innovations reset the state with probability r in (0,1], prescribing a state using that vertex innovation, and otherwise apply any fixed measurable function of the b child states and the local innovation. For a nonempty finite state space, if b(1-r)<=1, there is a unique compatible state assignment almost surely, the root is measurable from all innovations, and the distributional recursion has a unique fixed point. For b(1-r)<1, arbitrary depth-n boundary assignments disagree at the root with probability at most [b(1-r)]^n.
source_quote: Extend the interpretation/pivot theory when each vertex has iid auxiliary randomness and its state is a function of its child states and that local randomness.

label: proof; unreviewed
statement: Consider a stationary ergodic arrival stream of intensity lambda>0, job service requirements S>=0 at unit speed, and k identical servers. Jobs cannot receive service from multiple servers simultaneously, and every successful job must consume its full S units. If a stationary policy completes at least a fraction 1-q of arrivals within deadline D>0, then q>=P(S>D) and k>=lambda integral_0^(1-q) F_S^(-1)(u) du. The latter is a necessary capacity bound even if other jobs are abandoned; it is not a sufficient staffing rule.
source_quote: Find the minimum server count and a feasible scheduling policy that meet a prescribed response-time quantile under a specified stochastic workload.

label: proof; unreviewed
statement: For lambda>0,mu>0 and an integer c>lambda/mu, consider stationary FCFS M/M/c. Put a=c mu-lambda and let C be Erlang-C. For t>0, P(R>t)=exp(-mu t)+C mu [exp(-mu t)-exp(-a t)]/(a-mu) if a!=mu, and exp(-mu t)(1+C mu t) if a=mu. For every finite stable c this tail is strictly greater than exp(-mu t), and it tends to exp(-mu t) as c tends to infinity. Hence a finite FCFS staffing level meeting P(R>t)<=q exists exactly when q>exp(-mu t), for 0<=q<=1.
source_quote: Find the minimum server count and a feasible scheduling policy that meet a prescribed response-time quantile under a specified stochastic workload.

label: source-scope correction
statement: Drewitz and Ramirez, Selected topics in random walks in random environment, arXiv:1309.2589, Corollary 2.15, states that under ellipticity (E) and ergodicity (ERG), an invariant probability measure absolutely continuous with respect to the environment law yields an annealed almost-sure law of large numbers. If the walk is transient in a given direction, it is ballistic in that direction. Thus the unresolved implication in the cached Open question 2.19 is the converse, ballisticity implying existence of such an invariant probability measure. Present literature status is not certified by this offline check. The campaign already corrected this in C0040-A002; that correction supersedes C0040-A001.
source_quote: For a RWRE satisfying (ERG) and (E) and transient in a direction, is the existence of an invariant probability measure for the environmental process absolutely continuous with respect to P equivalent to ballisticity in that direction?

label: proof; unreviewed
statement: Let P be a shift-invariant law of nearest-neighbor environments on Z with 0<p_i<1 and rho_i=(1-p_i)/p_i. Define S_1=1+sum_{k>=1} product_{j=1}^k rho_j and Z=E_P[(1+rho_0)S_1]. If Z<infinity, then Q with density h=(1+rho_0)S_1/Z is an invariant probability measure for the environment kernel Kf=p_0 f(theta omega)+(1-p_0)f(theta^(-1)omega). It is equivalent to P and E_Q[2p_0-1]=1/Z>0. For iid rho with m=E rho<1, Z=(1+m)/(1-m). This is a known one-dimensional special case rederived here, not a general answer to C0040.
source_quote: For a RWRE satisfying (ERG) and (E) and transient in a direction, is the existence of an invariant probability measure for the environmental process absolutely continuous with respect to P equivalent to ballisticity in that direction?

label: proof; unreviewed
statement: In any finite open graph with connected distinct vertices u,v, let K be the number of open edges pivotal for u-v connectivity, and let d be the shortest open-path length. Then d>=K, sharply. A single open edge gives d=K=1, so d>=K+1 is false. On a fully open cycle of length 2L with opposite endpoints, K=0 and d=L; hence no uniform additive upper bound on d-K follows from pivotal count. Pointwise, {u connected to v,K>=N} is contained in {u connected to v,d>=N}, so pivotal tail bounds transfer as lower bounds for intrinsic tails, not as upper bounds.
source_quote: Extend the fixed-number-of-pivotals two-point function result (Theorem 15.4) to the intrinsic-distance two-point function tau_n^{(in)}(x) = P_{p_c}(d_{C(0)}(0,x) = n), d > 6.

label: proof; unreviewed
statement: Let X be a finite centered Gaussian vector, let X prime be an independent copy, and set Y=rho X+sqrt(1-rho^2)X prime for 0<=rho<=1. Let I(Y) be a deterministic measurable tie-broken maximizer of Y and m=E max_i X_i. Then D=max_i X_i-X_{I(Y)} is nonnegative and E D=(1-rho)m. Consequently P(D>delta)<=(1-rho)m/delta for every delta>0. No nonnegativity of off-diagonal covariances is required. This proves near-optimal height of a noised maximizer; it supplies no overlap or multiple-peaks guarantee.
source_quote: Show that chaos implies the multiple-peaks property for Gaussian fields whose correlations are not all nonnegative, which requires a second-moment bound on the overlap R(I_0, I_t) between the maximiser at time 0 and at time t.

label: proof; unreviewed
statement: For X=(Z,-Z), Z standard normal, and its Ornstein-Uhlenbeck copy Y=(Z_t,-Z_t), where Z_t=e^(-t)Z+sqrt(1-e^(-2t))Z prime, the covariance overlap R(I(X),I(Y)) equals 1 when the signs agree and -1 otherwise. Its mean is (2/pi)arcsin(e^(-t)), tending to zero as t tends to infinity, while its second moment is exactly one and P(R>1/2) tends to 1/2. Thus a small mean of a signed overlap alone cannot be used with Markov to conclude a small upper tail. This does not refute chaos-to-multiple-peaks at vanishing noise time for a sequence of fields.
source_quote: Show that chaos implies the multiple-peaks property for Gaussian fields whose correlations are not all nonnegative, which requires a second-moment bound on the overlap R(I_0, I_t) between the maximiser at time 0 and at time t.

label: proof; unreviewed
statement: In a four-person SIR model with irreversible removal and certain transmission on a listed contact, let A be initially infectious and allow contacts only A-C at time 0.1, A-B at 1, C-B at 9, and B-D at 10. Coupling iid rate-one exponential infectious lifetimes L_A,L_C,L_B to the longer lifetimes 3L_A,3L_C,3L_B gives positive probability that D is infected in the baseline process but never infected in the longer-lifetime process. Therefore this shared-lifetime coupling does not have pathwise inclusion of infected sets. This is a fixed-contact diagnostic, not a counterexample to Brownian SIR survival or survival monotonicity.
source_quote: Does the fully diffusing Poisson Brownian SIR model survive for sufficiently small positive removal rate when d>=2?

label: proof; unreviewed
statement: Let E be finite and T=E minus {J}, with any distribution q for J. For all increasing events A,B in the full edge-coordinate cube, P(A box B)<=P(A)P(B), where box is disjoint occurrence through coordinate certificates. Consequently BK holds for the weighted spanning-tree law on any finite connected unicyclic graph with strictly positive edge weights, for all increasing events.
source_quote: For increasing events A,B on edge subsets, is the probability of their disjoint occurrence under any weighted uniform spanning-tree law at most P(A)P(B)?
